memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'If your offering is a fellowship offering, and you offer an animal from the herd, whether male or female, you are to present before the LORD an animal without defect.'" - Lev 3:1 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A new offering begins here, and its name tells you everything. The Hebrew word is shelamim, from the same root as shalom — peace, wholeness, wellbeing. Older translations call it the peace offering. The NIV calls it the fellowship offering. Both are right, because peace with God leads to fellowship with God.

Here is what makes this offering different from the others: much of it was eaten. Not just by the priests, but by the worshipper and his family. This was the offering that ended in a shared meal in God's presence. It was worship that looked like dinner.

And notice the small phrase: whether male or female. In chapter 1 the burnt offering had to be male. Here God relaxes the requirement. Why? Because this offering is not chiefly about atonement — it is about celebration. The relationship is already established. Now comes the joy of it.

Some Christians know God only as someone to confess sin to. That is real, but it is not the whole. God also invites us to His table. Jesus said, "I have come that they may have life, and have it to the full" (Jn 10:10). Peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ (Rom 5:1) is not the end of the story. It is the beginning of the meal.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I relate to God mainly as a judge to be satisfied, or also as a Father to enjoy?
2. When did I last simply delight in God rather than only asking Him for things?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that peace with You leads to fellowship with You. Teach me not only to confess to You but to enjoy You. Amen.
